Bihar Cabinet approves Patna Metro expansion

Test Reporter | Patna, September 28

The Bihar Cabinet on Sunday approved the much-awaited expansion of the Patna Metro rail project, clearing two additional corridors covering the rapidly growing suburbs of Bihta and Fatuha.

Officials said the expanded network will add 28 kilometres of elevated and underground track to the existing Phase 1 corridors, taking the total sanctioned metro length in the state capital past 60 kilometres.

The Urban Development and Housing Department has been directed to submit the revised detailed project report within three months so that tenders can be invited early next year.

Transport economists welcomed the decision, noting that Patna's vehicular population has nearly doubled in a decade while road space has grown only marginally.

The Cabinet also approved budgetary support of Rs 750 crore as the state's share for land acquisition and utility shifting along the new corridors.

Construction on the priority corridor is expected to begin within eighteen months of tender award, officials added.
